newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Status quo prevails on NYMEX oil futures.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Status quo prevails on NYMEX oil futures.

text.p: The status quo is likely to prevail for NYMEX crude and product futures in the short term with trendline support and resistance levels appearing stronger than the market's current conviction to break them, analysts said on Wednesday.
"(NYMEX crude) is flirting with a trendline that coincides at $19.44, This could act as a pivot point for today's activity," GNI Research said in their daily report.
NYMEX crude has been trading into the apex of a bearish pennant formation.

That was formed by a long term downtrend line stemming from December 19s $26.80 high and an uptrend line from June 20s $18.35 low on the spot month chart, these two lines cross over at around $19.44 .
However, trading is expected to be slow with a break in any direction limited by thin volume trade.
Fenella Graham at MeesPierson said "Preparation remains neutral so we would look to buy at $19.25 or another buying extreme while taking profits and going short on a scale up basis from $19.60-86".
"A break of the bottom range and we cut length but we cannot join any breaks until the volume improves," she added.
A succession of long legged Doji candlesticks on the spot month gasoline chart continue to flag 'market uncertainty, according to Japanese candlestick charting techniques.
Analysts said the market looked volatile to the downside as it continues to bump off quite good support from a short term uptrend line and with momentum indicators turning negative.
"The medium term trend is for lower numbers but in the short term there could be some support for NYMEX products today which will spill over into crude". GNI said.

Heating oil futures are still seen moving sideways with a short term downtrend line from May 16's 58.90 cent high capping any upside movement and restricting the market to narrow range trading, though there is little strong support to the downside before 50.70 cents.
